symptom: A `custom name map` name (or an `item of` name) that Mendix refuses, such as '1bad', 'has space', 'Owner', 'class' or an empty string, passed `check` and `exec` and was written; `mx check` reported CE9524 "JSON element '(Object)/name' has an invalid custom name".
file: mdl/executor/validate_json_structure_names.go validCustomName and invalidCustomNameViolations (MDL-JSON03). Tests validate_json_structure_names_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/json-structure-invalid-custom-name.fail.mdl and json-structure-custom-names.mdl
cause: The earlier CE9524 findings were about GENERATED names (`$type`, `owner`, `%3A`) and were fixed by sanitising the default name, which is why a bare structure now builds clean; an explicit custom name is written verbatim and nothing judged it.
insight: **Re-measure an old finding's symptom before building on it: the class had moved.** Three records said CE9524 came from member names, and a fresh matrix showed every such member now builds clean (the default is sanitised). What remained was the author's own custom name, which is written verbatim. The accepted set was measured over 90 names rather than assumed from the message text: ASCII only (Größe, naïve are refused although they are letters), a lone underscore is refused, and the reserved list is the SAME case-insensitive one the platform uses for CE7247, so types.IsPlatformReserved is reused instead of a second list; String, System, Value, Entity, Date, List and User are not reserved. Every word of PlatformReservedWords and SystemAttributeNames was rejected in the second measurement, so the shared list is safe to reuse here.
